one_liner: Rust linter and formatter replacing Flake8, Black, isort, pyupgrade, and more with one fast CLI.
what_it_does: Ruff lints and formats Python code, replacing Flake8 plus dozens of plugins, Black, isort, pydocstyle, pyupgrade, and autoflake with a single Rust binary. It ships as a pip-installable CLI (`ruff check`, `ruff format`) configured via pyproject.toml, plus a language server (ruff_server) for editors, and natively re-implements ~900 rules including popular Flake8 plugins like flake8-bugbear. The linter is a near drop-in for Flake8 only under specific conditions (few/no plugins, used alongside a formatter, Python 3 code); the formatter targets near-identical output to Black on already-Black-formatted code.
how_it_is_fast: Written in Rust and shipped as a single native binary, it avoids the per-file Python interpreter and plugin-subprocess overhead that Flake8's plugin architecture incurs; rules are natively re-implemented in Rust rather than shelled out to separate Python checkers. It also has built-in result caching so unchanged files are skipped on incremental runs. CONTRIBUTING.md's own benchmark shows most of the incremental win comes from that cache: a cold lint of CPython takes ~294ms, a cached rerun ~48ms.
when_to_use: Python 3 codebase already on Flake8 with few/no exotic plugins, run alongside a formatter
Want one tool for both linting and Black-style formatting instead of two separate ones
Large codebases or monorepos where whole-repo lint/format time matters in CI or pre-commit
Need editor/LSP integration (VS Code and others via ruff_server) with fast on-save checks
Want built-in autofix for import sorting, unused imports, and pyupgrade-style modernization in one pass
when_not_to_use: Team depends on specific Flake8 plugins Ruff hasn't re-implemented natively
Need output byte-identical to Black on code that wasn't already Black-formatted (FAQ notes more deviation there)
Need full Pylint parity; coverage is partial and some Pylint-style rule requests are still open
Using `--extend-per-file-ignores` together with leading recursive glob patterns — open issue reports an extreme performance penalty (#8626)
Autofixes for PERF401/PERF403 rules have open bug reports of making code slower in some cases (#21890, #21891) — review fixes before accepting

integration.form: CLI binary (installed via pip/pipx/uv/cargo); source is a Rust crate workspace (crates/*)
integration.dependencies: none for the prebuilt binary (self-contained, no Python runtime required to run it)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.96 (edition 2024) to build from source; prebuilt wheels declare Python >=3.7 as the package requirement
integration.platforms: PyPI classifier lists 'OS Independent'; wheels are published for common platforms but no explicit CPU-architecture list was found this session
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — linter is drop-in for Flake8 only with few/no plugins, used alongside a formatter, on Python 3 code; formatter is drop-in for Black with near-identical output on already-Black-formatted code, more deviation otherwise

gotchas: Formatting non-Black-formatted code produces more diffs than the near-100% match figure implies (FAQ)
`--extend-per-file-ignores` combined with leading recursive glob patterns triggers an 'extreme performance penalty' (issue #8626, open)
PERF401/PERF403 autofix suggestions have open bug reports of producing slower code in some cases (#21890, #21891)
Ruff's linter and Black/ruff-format treat line-length enforcement differently, so E501 can still fire even with the formatter enabled
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No catalogued sibling targets Python lint/format specifically: Biome and Oxlint are the JS/TS equivalents (ESLint/Prettier), Pyrefly and ty are Python type-checkers (a different job than linting/formatting), and clangd-tidy is the C/C++ equivalent. Pick Ruff whenever the baseline being replaced is Flake8, Black, isort, or pylint on a Python codebase.
verified_claims_summary: CONTRIBUTING.md's reproducible hyperfine benchmark (Ruff release build vs. the CPython 3.10 tree, pinned tool versions, Python 3.11) shows Ruff at 294ms cold vs Flake8 12.26s (41.66x), pyflakes 15.79s (53.64x), pycodestyle 46.92s (159.43x), and autoflake 6.18s (20.98x) — but states no CPU model. The larger headline figures (~150x vs Flake8, ~60ms incremental re-lint) come from the founder's 2022 blog post on unspecified macOS hardware, not this repo benchmark; the Black formatting-speed claim appears only in the README, with no benchmark numbers given anywhere.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-24, 49,764 stars, MIT license); copyable either as a pip-installed prebuilt binary or as a vendorable Rust crate workspace, so there's little build/toolchain risk for adopters.
